title: Identity hardening + data residency & SSO review - Oceanside Pharma
summary: Introductory security alignment: SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning design, RBAC/least-privilege patterns, KMS key wrapping and envelope encryption, audit log retention & export to SIEM, and data residency constraints for EU clinical data. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 + ISO certs, network diagram for private deployment, run a short scoping pilot for SCIM role mapping, and schedule an on-prem install workshop.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Recorders: Fireflies
Attendees: Ellen Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jon Alvarez (Redwood SA); Dr. Rina Patel (Head of Security, Oceanside), Liam O'Rourke (Cloud Infra), Sanjay Mehta (Platform Ops), Hannah Ruiz (Legal)

[00:00] Ellen (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick agenda — SSO + SCIM, role design, encryption/KMS questions, audit logs, and the residency constraints for the EU clinical projects. is that okay?
[00:12] Rina (Oceanside): yes, thanks Ellen. we have a few compliance checkpoints — SOC2 scope includes backups and log retention, and we need to confirm where PHI-adjacent artifacts land.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): great — we'll call out the hosted vs dedicated vs private diffs as we go, and highlight what we normally recommend for regulated workloads.
[00:28] Liam: quick thing, we are running in azure EU regions primarily, and we have a dedicated VNet. any private deployment would need VNet peering or express route; we prefer no egress to non-EU.
[00:38] Jon (Redwood): noted. we'll map options: Redwood Hosted (data in region), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in a cloud region), Redwood Private (customer VPC or on-prem).
[00:46] Rina: also SSO — we use an internal IdP (Azure AD). we need SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role mapping. minimal scope: engineers get read/test access, platform ops get deploy privileges, security gets audit access only.
[00:58] Maya: ok, SCIM can sync groups -> roles. two gotchas we've seen: 1) group nesting in AD sometimes doesn't map cleanly to our flat role model, 2) SAML assertion attributes and audience fields need to be consistent or the login fails after the first bind.
[01:12] Liam: nesting is real for us. we map teams to nested groups. can Redwood's SCIM handle nested groups or will we need a bridge?
[01:20] Maya: currently, SCIM v2 support is for group membership enumeration; nested group flattening is left to the IdP. many customers implement an Azure AD provisioning rule that expands nested groups into a flat group claim for SCIM. we can document a recommended mapping snippet.
[01:34] Rina: that would be helpful. second, about RBAC — least privilege is a must. we're concerned about token reuse and broad service accounts. can we do short-lived session tokens and granular API keys per route?
[01:48] Jon: yes — Redwood issues API keys per service account. for elevated operations we recommend integrating with your KMS-backed short-lived credentials or using our SSO session integration. our private deployment supports short TTLs and ephemeral workload tokens.
[02:02] Sanjay: speaking of KMS, do you bring your own key (BYOK)? we have HSM-backed keys in Azure Key Vault.
[02:10] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration. envelope encryption is applied to persisted artifacts. small caveat: for Hosted, we manage keys unless customer opts into a dedicated key in a bring-your-key arrangement; for Dedicated you can have a KM IP endpoint in your VNet. sometimes docs say KMSes or K-M-Ses in transcripts, so apologies for typos.
[02:28] Rina: we need a clear statement that data-at-rest for EU clinical projects never leaves region and that keys are stored in EU key vaults.
[02:36] Ellen: agreed. for Private deployments we can ensure keys and storage are in the same EU region; we'll include region binding language in the MSA and the runbook for the pilot.
[02:46] Hannah (Legal): we'll need explicit audit language and sub-processor detail. also confirm retention windows for logs and backups.
[02:54] Jon: audit logs — Redwood can export audit trails (admin actions, API calls, model selection, prompts metadata) to your SIEM via syslog or secure S3 export. retention is configurable. typical pattern: 90 days in the system, and long-term exports to your archival S3 in the region for 7 years if required.
[03:12] Rina: 90 days is fine short-term but for compliance we need 7 years of certain telemetry. can you confirm the export pipeline is encrypted in transit and at rest?
[03:22] Maya: yes — TLS for in-transit; exports are encrypted with envelope encryption and can be re-wrapped by your key. we'll provide the export manifest and the transfer certificate expectations.
[03:32] Liam: on the network side, private deployment: do you support VNet peering + private endpoints, or do we need an express route?
[03:38] Jon: both options exist. VNet peering is common for cloud-hosted private nodes; for on-prem we support an agent-based connector and an express-route/ha tunnels. for PCI/PHI we often start with express-route or direct connect equivalents.
[03:50] Rina: audit trail integrity is important — do you provide tamper-evident logs or signed snapshots?
[03:56] Maya: we provide append-only logs with integrity checks and a signed daily snapshot option. those snapshots can be rotated into your long-term store. we also provide hashes for key artifacts.
[04:08] Sanjay: about SCIM role mapping, can we define custom role attributes? we have multiple permission slices per team (read, run-poc, promote).
[04:16] Maya: yes — Redwood supports custom role definitions. SCIM can provision a role attribute on a user like 'role:platform:promote' but the IdP must be configured to send the group->role mapping claim or we can use provisioning rules. we'll share a sample claim config for Azure AD.
[04:32] Rina: also, is there support for just-in-time (JIT) elevated access for audits? sometimes we need to grant temporary 'security:viewer' or 'platform:ops' for 4 hours.
[04:44] Jon: we support time-bound role grants via our console/integration — you can request escalation and it issues an ephemeral token tied to an audit entry. we can also integrate with your existing PAM if you want approval flows.
[04:56] Hannah: make sure the approval and escalation flows are logged for later review — legal wants the chain.
[05:02] Maya: absolutely — every elevation generates an audit event with requester, approver, TTL, and justification field.
[05:10] Speaker 1 (background): mm-hmm
[05:12] Ellen: switching to SAML details — typical gotchas: NameID formats, audience restriction, ACS URL trailing slashes, and certificate rollovers. we've seen logins break when the IdP rotates certs and the SP metadata wasn't updated.
[05:26] Liam: do you support SAML metadata auto-refresh?
[05:30] Maya: we can configure automatic metadata polling for some IdPs or we recommend using an intermediatory like AD FS or AAD - conditional access is still on your side.
[05:38] Rina: SCIM provisioning frequency? we don't want a lag of 30 minutes when a user is revoked.
[05:44] Maya: provisioning intervals are configurable. default is 40 minutes on hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we can push near real-time via webhooks or an event-driven connector. many customers run a shorter interval of 5 minutes for sensitive teams.
[05:56] Sanjay: ok we'll want 5 minute provisioning for security groups.
[06:00] Ellen: about secrets — do you have secrets scanning or token revocation API?
[06:06] Jon: yes — tokens can be revoked via API, and we have a secrets scanning runner for stored prompts/attachments. we can include a scrubber that detects PHI-like patterns as part of your onboarding eval, but it's not a compliance guarantee.
[06:20] Rina: SOC2/ISO — can you share scope, dates, and auditor? and also the penetration test summary?
[06:26] Ellen: yes we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO attestation, plus a pen test executive summary. also our compliance pack has a subprocessor list and data flow diagram.
[06:36] Hannah: please annotate the diagrams with where PHI-adjacent data may be persisted. we need this for our DPO.
[06:44] Maya: will do — we'll mark the interfaces and show encryption boundaries.
[06:48] Rina: one more: legal — is there an option to have contractual region locks in the MSA to prevent cross-border transfers?
[06:56] Ellen: yes — for Private we can include region lock clauses and for Dedicated we can lock customer data to specific regions and disallow fallback to other regions. we'll draft proposed language.
[07:06] Jon: we should also call out fallback behavior — e.g., if a region loses capacity we can failover to a compatible EU region only, never to non-EU, if that's a hard requirement.
[07:18] Liam: network diagrams for the on-prem connector + required open ports would be useful.
[07:24] Maya: we'll attach the network guide and a sample iptables/NSG rule set.
[07:28] Sanjay: any E2E encryption for in-flight prompts between client and Redwood? we need assurances prompts are encrypted and not stored unless explicitly persisted.
[07:36] Jon: TLS 1.2/1.3 for transport, and by default prompts are transient in memory; for persisted prompts or audits we apply envelope encryption. we can also offer masking at ingestion for specific fields.
[07:50] Rina: what's the retention policy for KV cache and model caches? anything stored to speed up generation could be considered sensitive.
[07:58] Maya: KV cache is ephemeral and typically memory-only for inference; we do not persist KV cache unless you opt into a warm-start feature. any persisted artifacts are subject to the same region/key rules. sometimes transcripts transcribed as KV cash in notes, ignore that.
[08:12] Hannah: regarding subpoenas or legal holds: do you have a process to freeze and export customer data on request?
[08:20] Ellen: yes — we have a legal escalation path and data export tooling. we'll provide the legal request playbook and SLA for data exports.
[08:30] Rina: okay thanks. can you summarise the practical actions for our team?
[08:34] Ellen: sure — immediate items: 1) we'll send SOC2/ISO + pen test exec summary, 2) SCIM config snippet for Azure AD with group flattening rules, 3) network diagram + port list for private connector, 4) sample role mapping and claim config, 5) proposed MSA clause for region binding.
[08:52] Rina: good. we also want a short pilot: SCIM provisioning + role mapping for the platform ops team and a test of log export to our SIEM.
[08:58] Jon: propose a 2-week pilot: week 1 config + dry-run in non-prod EU region, week 2 run SIEM export and do elevation exercises.
[09:06] Liam: that timeline works. can you include estimated cost for Dedicated vs Private and any infra egress costs?
[09:12] Ellen: yes we'll include a rough TCO comparison and note any egress charges.
[09:18] Sanjay: also would like a demo of the ephemeral elevation flow and revoke token call.
[09:22] Maya: we can demo that in the pilot kickoff.
[09:26] Hannah: legal will review proposed MSA language once we get the draft.
[09:30] Ellen: excellent. any final questions?
[09:34] Rina: none from me, thanks.
[09:36] Liam: none.
[09:38] Ellen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff next week.
[09:44] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional auto-transcription errors for acronyms and product names (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'KMSes' spelled 'K-M-Ses') and some speaker attribution uncertainty near minute marks.
